_about: What a reader must find in the v1.4 fixtures. Written BY HAND from tests/v14-fixtures/make_sources.py and tests/make_v14_fixtures.sh (the data given to the real tools), and checked against the files with independent tools (Python sqlite3, zipfile, pdf.js text positions) on 2026-11-02. NOT produced by any DataBrief reader: it is the oracle of the v1.4 tests.

avro.note: the same records in every codec: a reader must give identical rows for the 4 files

tables.note: merged header: 'Quarter' spans the last two columns; first row Region | Quarter (merged), second row '' | Q1 | Q2, third North | 10 | 12

docx.informational: headings and paragraphs are text, the 3 tables are the data

files.report.pdf: LibreOffice Writer: 1 page, the 3 tables of report.docx (cells that wrap become several text lines)
files.deck.pdf: LibreOffice Impress: 3 pages, the orders table on page 2
files.orders-chrome.pdf: Chrome (Skia/PDF): 1 page, one table of 4 rows

pdf.note: tables in a PDF are GUESSED from text positions: a reader must label them as such

plainTextOnly.note: a pandas Series (groupby sum): text/plain only, no HTML table

ipynb.neverRun: a reader must never execute anything: only the stored outputs are read

ipynbShapes.data: sales: region, year, amount, qty = North 2023 10.5 3 / North 2024 12.0 4 / South 2023 7.25 2 / South 2024 9.0 5

tables.by_region: named index 'region' (set_index): a column of its own
tables.pivot: MultiIndex columns: amount / 2023, amount / 2024, qty / 2023, qty / 2024; index 'region'
tables.two_levels: MultiIndex rows region, year (rowspan in the HTML)
tables.wide: 30 columns c0..c29, pandas stores c0..c9 and c20..c29 with a '...' column between; footer '3 rows × 30 columns'
tables.first, second: two display() calls in one cell
tables.pl_sales: Polars: a row of types (str, f64) in the head, text in quotes, 'shape: (2, 2)'

ipynbShapes.other: stderr text and a PNG image in cell 9; cell 10 added after the run (never executed)

gpkg.note: a GeoPackage is a SQLite file: the gpkg_* and rtree_* tables are its own machinery, not user data

canary.markers: CONFIDENTIAL_REC (records: never), CONFIDENTIAL_TEXT (titles, paragraphs, headings, notes, metadata, code, markdown: only when free text is allowed), CONFIDENTIAL_COL (names: only when names are shared), CONFIDENTIAL_FILE (the file name)
canary.pdfFragments: in PDFs a long marker can be cut where the cell wraps (CONFIDENTIAL_REC_ + 01, CONFIDENTIAL_TEXT_TITL + E): the no-share tests must look for the fragments CONFIDENTIAL_REC, CONFIDENTIAL_TEXT and CONFIDENTIAL_COL, not only whole markers
